reviewer: GPT-6.1 Sol, user-selected Max; independent coherent-case evaluator
coverage_meaning: Every material current assertion in the complete report, including all findings, mechanisms, exceptions, counters, unresolved decisions, plan alternatives/rejections/improvements, every proposed fixture and all six facets, was assessed. No sampling.

claims.claim: Case/date/version/fixed source hash, size, line count, aliases and read-only local synthetic brief/plan scope.
claims.reason: The input identities are pinned and match; V001 is the visible current label, not proof of no earlier native versions.

claims.claim: Cache before model exposure, one six-chunk source pass, zero rereads, Q1 before Q2, native Goal and permitted-tool compliance, self-reported logs and no prior versions.
claims.reason: Native cache/read/Goal/protocol/acquisition operations and earlier-version inventory are not supplied. Current process claims cannot be verified from final text; no receipt or cost inference is credited.

claims.claim: RFC keywords, lowercase use, normative-text exceptions, epistemic labels, capture-scoped negatives and UNEXECUTED proposals.
claims.reason: The framework is broadly correct; individual applications and exhaustive negative claims are reviewed separately.

claims.claim: Zarr v3, allowed features unless disallowed, adoption date, possible valid codec/transformer data beyond reader support.
claims.reason: The explicit exception is retained and no unsupported native codec coverage is claimed. A limited reader needs a disclosed capability boundary.

claims.claim: The source disallows almost nothing and does not enumerate real producer features.
claims.reason: No explicit codec/transformer ban is identified, but meaningful axis, transform and label-type restrictions do exist. A real feature-emission landscape remains unverified; one downscaling method/version is described.

claims.claim: attributes.ome and string hierarchy-consistent version; inconsistent metadata is invalid and can be detected.
claims.reason: The source defines conformance; validation/feedback implementation remains a product responsibility.

claims.claim: Real JSON must omit comments; identified commented examples cannot be copied unchanged.
claims.reason: The explicit commented examples contain a copying trap. This does not make every uncommented example malformed.

claims.claim: Local/HTTP/object-store storage neutrality; local-only product is a disclosed subset.
claims.reason: The storage scope matches the brief; remote support is not required for this product.

claims.claim: Image groups, separate level arrays, arbitrary names, axes/rank/type ordering, chunk specification; numbered collection exception is conditional.
claims.reason: Folder or conventional axis names are not a reliable semantic source. omero optionality is correctly restored in F18.

claims.claim: Nested labels and intermediates; mandatory integer whitelist and no metadata in intermediate groups.
claims.reason: These normative constraints are correctly identified; floating labels and metadata-bearing intermediates are genuine invalid-input cases.

claims.claim: The illustrative label-dimension should statement is normative solely because lowercase RFC terms retain force.
claims.reason: Lowercase force does not override the exception for examples/layout commentary. At most this is useful weak correspondence guidance, not a universal mandatory grid relationship.

claims.claim: HCS requires well/row/plate hierarchy and corresponding specifications, with empty groups SHOULD NOT, only when the dataset is HCS.
claims.reason: The scope condition is explicit, avoiding a universal HCS requirement.

claims.claim: Axis names required and unique; types/units recommended, custom strings allowed, rank identity mandatory.
claims.reason: The core name/rank and recommendation distinctions are correct.

claims.claim: Names, types and units are only SHOULD-level except name presence/uniqueness.
claims.reason: The exception correctly identifies mandatory name presence/uniqueness, but saying names are only SHOULD is confusing and should be limited to type/unit recommendations. No fixed-name mandate is inferred.

claims.claim: dimension_names is required on each level array and matches group axes; historical clarification and locus difference.
claims.reason: The important array-versus-group locus is accurately explained.

claims.claim: Multiscales has rank 2–5, two or three spaces, optional one time and one channel/custom slot, and metadata/array type ordering.
claims.reason: The rank/order/optional slot interpretation is grounded and scoped within each dictionary.

claims.claim: All three-space stacks SHOULD use zyx; axis-order violations make mapping ill-posed.
claims.reason: The source specifies yx image-plane and other anisotropic z-axis conditions. Incorrect array/metadata ordering violates conformance, though a known nonstandard order can be mathematically mapped if truthfully declared; invalidity is not universal mathematical impossibility.

claims.claim: Required dataset list, group-relative arbitrary paths, declared highest-resolution order, same rank/order matching axes within dictionary.
claims.reason: This validates metadata authority without imposing fixed ratios or names. It does not eliminate a need to check actual arrays/geometry.

claims.claim: One dataset scale with physical size normally, conditional relative-factor/default fallback, optional translation after scale and matching vector lengths.
claims.reason: The unavailable/inapplicable absolute-scaling condition and no-downsampling fallback are accurately retained.

claims.claim: Optional group transforms follow dataset transforms under the same rules; ordered composition and worked time factor.
claims.reason: The composition order is correct. Identity is a general/no-op default; explicit identity is not an allowed dataset multiscales transform.

claims.claim: Inline or container binary path vectors are allowed; inline-only without detection cannot support all such data.
claims.reason: A correct capability inference, with unsupported data explicitly disclosed rather than silently miscalibrated.

claims.claim: Multiple entry choice by name/first fallback and chunk-size comment; exact conformance force is unresolved.
claims.reason: The passage supplies descriptive entry-selection guidance and code, not a universal required chooser. The chunk-size comment chooses a multiscales entry rather than a dataset pyramid level; later implications must preserve that distinction.

claims.claim: name/type/downscaling metadata SHOULD be present and are not mandatory keys.
claims.reason: Recommended descriptive fields are correctly separated from required geometry.

claims.claim: Optional transitional omero with conditional channels/RGB/window fields; example-only rdefs and full external semantics unverified.
claims.reason: Conditional key/field obligations are accurate; arbitrary initial rendering behavior is not imposed as a source MUST.

claims.claim: All channel colors/windows/defaults exist only when omero is present.
claims.reason: As metadata location this is reasonable, but rdefs/defaults are illustrative and not guaranteed by mere omero presence; a viewer can also choose its own absent-metadata display defaults.

claims.claim: Required label paths with all-label completeness SHOULD; label multiscales must have source-equal level count, not necessarily identical shapes.
claims.reason: The count-versus-shape distinction is explicit. It still does not resolve actual source identity or registration.

claims.claim: image-label and colors/version presence SHOULD; conditional array/string/ID/RGBA types and reader color preference SHOULD.
claims.reason: The nested presence/type distinction and palette recommendation are correctly retained.

claims.claim: Optional properties/source, keyed IDs, arbitrary nonuniform metadata, relative source reference/default and unenumerated version strings.
claims.reason: These are correct metadata facts. Describing source as an optional extra does not supply a validated association before rendering.

claims.claim: Required complete physical row/column lists, unique case-sensitive names, recommended filesystem caution, plate version and consistent well path/indexes.
claims.reason: The path/index and empty-grid-versus-populated-well distinctions are accurate.

claims.claim: Acquisition optional; IDs unique nonnegative, recommended name/maximumfieldcount and conditional string/integer types; field_count/name recommended.
claims.reason: The recommendation/presence/types and source field_count phrasing are preserved.

claims.claim: Dense two-acquisition plate and sparse 12×8 grid with two wells are source examples.
claims.reason: Examples establish possible fixtures, not an obligation to present a particular grid UI.

claims.claim: Required well fields/path uniqueness; acquisition reference only with multiple plate acquisitions; version SHOULD with conditional string.
claims.reason: Conditional acquisition and plate/well version strengths are correct.

claims.claim: Transitional real-world collection layout 3, optional series string paths with XML-order condition, plate locations and numeric fallback without both series and plate.
claims.reason: Both key discovery conditions are retained; no cross-version pixel-storage inference follows from transitional metadata alone.

claims.claim: Plate takes precedence and collection/plate mixing is disallowed.
claims.reason: Top-level conditionality and exclusivity are supported.

claims.claim: If XML is provided it must follow OME-XML/MetadataOnly, with minimum spec allowed.
claims.reason: The content rules are conditional on supplied XML; presence is separately recommended in F24.

claims.claim: Reader SHOULD disclose multiple images and not silently first-open; MAY use series, all/choice display or ignore roots.
claims.reason: The report retains source SHOULD/MAY strength.

claims.claim: Exact legacy key spellings and potential future naming updates should be version-pinned.
claims.reason: Exact spellings are current facts; watching future changes is a proposed engineering measure, not proof a particular rename has happened.

claims.claim: Released version, migration promise, draft uncertainty, hierarchy and plate/well version differences, v3 and separator history.
claims.reason: The cited historical statements and modal differences are present.

claims.claim: Per-level arrays/declared ordering permit multiresolution navigation; level choice is reader policy.
claims.reason: A valid mechanism inference without a fixed reduction ratio claim.

claims.claim: Sequential scale/translation composition, conditional relative default and optional dataset-then-group mapping.
claims.reason: The previously stated relative fallback condition applies; no universal physical-unit guarantee is asserted here.

claims.claim: Metadata-driven plate/collection/image/label discovery and arbitrary axis/array names.
claims.reason: A useful discovery outline, scoped to the recognized layouts.

claims.claim: Chunks enable partial loading, while detailed addressing/codec costs remain external.
claims.reason: This is an engineering feasibility argument rather than measured performance.

claims.claim: No specified invalid-input runtime error/recovery/warning protocol in the fixed source; defaults/precedence/entry choice are listed.
claims.reason: Full-source review supports this specific absence. Product feedback and native operation are not format guarantees.

claims.claim: There is no format-sanctioned way to distinguish invalid from valid but unsupported; viewer defines the boundary itself.
claims.reason: The format defines invalidity through mandatory constraints and permits features beyond a reader capability profile. The viewer defines support breadth, not conformance validity itself. Runtime error policy is indeed open.

claims.claim: Transitional/read-write, unit/type/custom, optional translations/groups, conditional acquisition/XML, recommended labels, and empty-grid conditions remain attached.
claims.reason: This useful consolidated condition list is substantially accurate; it does not establish full facet coverage.

claims.claim: Transitional 0.4-era/v2-style data is counterevidence to v3-only viewing and may occur in the wild.
claims.reason: Earlier-layout metadata can be part of current v3/0.5 data. The source does not establish v2 for all 0.4 data or require older pixel-storage support. Older compatibility may be a product choice, but the counterargument overextends metadata continuity.

claims.claim: Examples can include prohibited real-data comments, creating fixture-copy pitfalls.
claims.reason: The specific identified commented examples support the warning.

claims.claim: No reader/library implementation evidence or evidence of which libraries exist is in the corpus.
claims.reason: Actual reader tolerance and complete library support matrices are unverified. The source nonetheless names Bio-Formats/bioformats2raw and skimage with method/version information. A zero-evidence claim about all tools/libraries is too broad.

claims.claim: Zarr mechanics and exact read granularity are not captured; formal references list only RFC2119, with a separator-history note.
claims.reason: The formal reference list and detailed-mechanics limit are correct; an external reference does not verify all dependency semantics.

claims.claim: Full OMERO window/rdefs semantics require unadmitted WebGateway documentation.
claims.reason: The source defines RGB and basic window field meanings, but no complete display/initialization algorithm or start/end range relationship.

claims.reason: No unit conversion/grammar implementation is admitted; unit handling needs an explicit profile.

claims.claim: Compose dataset then group scale/offsets, disclose unknown units, and implement or detect/refuse binary vectors.

claims.claim: Declared level order/arbitrary names and selection heuristic are separate from multiple named entry choice.
claims.reason: Level heuristics are product choices; entry names do not replace the dataset list.

claims.claim: The multiscales chunk-size code comment is a hint for pyramid-level selection.
claims.reason: The code returns a multiscales list entry (for example multiscales[0]), not one of that entry’s datasets. It cannot be cited as a level-selection heuristic.

claims.claim: Validate overlay shape/count rather than assume same shapes; check integer dtype and recommended colors, define fallback.
claims.reason: Read-time validation and the weaker shape condition are improvements. Actual relative source association and coordinate transforms must also be resolved; properties/source cannot be treated as merely cosmetic extras for associated overlays.

claims.claim: Keep background/cancellation as engineering; external chunk/codec details prevent read-cost guarantees; disclose supported features.
claims.reason: No measured responsiveness or native supported codec set is claimed.

claims.reason: These mandatory surfaces can support the product feedback promise; no source runtime protocol is invented.

claims.claim: Local read-only scope fits, target version and transitional stance need pinning, real-tool interop remains untested.
claims.reason: The product boundary and untested status are sound. Tool-information absence and inferred v2 legacy storage are separately qualified above.

claims.claim: Existing library versus minimal custom reader is an option requiring future verified support matrices.
claims.reason: No specific library is recommended as proven capable; blanket no-library evidence is separately qualified.

claims.reason: These are legitimate product alternatives, but the cited chunk-size comment concerns entry selection rather than a pyramid level.

claims.reason: An explicit capability limit is preferable to silently miscalibrated output; no native operation is proved.

claims.claim: HCS full navigator versus detect-and-explain are product scope alternatives, sparse plates valid.
claims.reason: The format constraints do not themselves mandate broad GUI scope.

claims.claim: Strict validation versus disclosed best effort is a product choice; source supplies no invalid-input recovery algorithm.
claims.reason: The source validity rules remain authoritative; the accepted capability/recovery policy is product work.

claims.reason: The rejection and exact exception are supported.

claims.claim: Reject copying specification examples verbatim because they embed comments.
claims.reason: The rule applies to identified commented examples, not every example. Stripping explanatory comments before validating JSON is necessary for those examples; uncommented examples are not invalid for that reason.
